facility_roles.quote: The initial experiments operating at the 4 collision regions of PETRA were the JADE [28], Mark-J [29], PLUTO [31] and TASSO [30] detectors.

intervals.label: proposal recommended for approval
intervals.note: The PETRA Research Committee recommended five proposals for approval in October 1976; the source does not give a separate approval or construction date for this experiment. The interval runs to the start of data taking in January 1979; Table 1 has the Mark-J, PLUTO and TASSO detectors moved into the beam in October 1978.
intervals.quote: October: 5 proposals recommended for approval (CELLO, JADE, Mark-J, PLUTO, TASSO)

intervals.label: PETRA data taking
intervals.locator: DESY backgrounder "The discovery of the gluon"; end from Bethke & Wagner (2022), Table 1
intervals.note: Start = January 1979 data-taking (the detector was moved into the beam in October 1978); end = the 3 November 1986 final shutdown of PETRA and its experiments.
intervals.quote: Data-taking started in January 1979 by the detectors MARK J, PLUTO and TASSO.

intervals.label: PETRA shut down; experiment ended
intervals.note: All PETRA experiments ended with the final shutdown of PETRA as a collider.

name: TASSO
notes: No TASSO website was found; no URL is recorded.

The DESY backgrounder lists the collaboration as DESY with institutes from Aachen, Bonn, Hamburg, Imperial College, Oxford, the Rutherford Laboratory, the Weizmann Institute and Wisconsin; this is the 1979 composition, not a complete membership history.

physics_goals.quote: Hence an electron-positron collision that gives rise to a gluon ought to be characterised by three clearly distinct jets of particles inside the detector.
physics_goals.value: Search for hard gluon bremsstrahlung in e+e- annihilation, seen as events with three distinct jets in one plane

summary.plain: One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider in Hamburg. In 1979 its collaboration identified the first three-jet events, the first direct evidence of the gluon, the carrier of the strong force. It took data until PETRA closed in 1986.
summary.technical: TASSO, one of the five collaborations recommended for approval at PETRA in October 1976 (with CELLO, JADE, MARK J, PLUTO); located in PETRA's South-Eastern experimental hall; DESY plus the Universities of Aachen, Bonn and Hamburg, Imperial College, Oxford, the Rutherford Laboratory, the Weizmann Institute and the University of Wisconsin. Data-taking January 1979 to 3 November 1986; three-jet events shown in June 1979.
